bear: More investors doubt that the huge spending on AI will pay off, and the index leans heavily on tech companies.
Oil hit a six-month high because of the Middle East conflict, and airline stocks like United, Delta and American fell on worries about higher fuel costs.
Investors worry that higher oil prices will keep prices rising for everyone and push the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) to raise interest rates, which makes borrowing money cost more.
bull: 83% of the 111 S&P 500 companies that had reported so far earned more than experts predicted.
Few people were signing up for unemployment money, which shows the job market is holding steady.
Not all tech stocks fell: SailPoint, Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks each rose more than 7% on Friday after a survey showed companies plan to spend more on online security.

briefs.summary: The S&P 500 fell about 0.5% in the week ending Oct 23 and closed near 7,624. On Thursday, earnings reports from big companies (reports on how much money they made) made investors worry that businesses are spending too much on AI. That day the tech-heavy Nasdaq index had its biggest one-day drop since early June. On Friday, the S&P 500 lost another 0.5% and the Dow fell more than 600 points as oil reached a six-month high because of fears that fighting in the Middle East would get worse.

bear: The index fell 2.6% on Oct 22, its worst day since June, because of fears that AI companies are spending too much. Meta dropped about 7% even though its results beat expectations.
Oil prices rose to about $117, which weighed on stocks ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting. The Fed is the U.S. central bank that sets interest rates.
The Nasdaq is trading below its 100-day average price, which some traders read as sellers being in control. The Nasdaq 100 is also down 7.5% from its high for the year.
bull: Company results this season have been strong overall, and Nvidia and Micron reported some of their best numbers as demand for AI chips and memory rose.
On Monday, Oct 19, the Nasdaq rose 1.1% as investors bought tech stocks after they had fallen, which shows buyers are still interested.
The Nasdaq is still about 4% above its 200-day average (the average price over roughly the last 10 months), so its longer-term trend has not broken down.

briefs.summary: The Nasdaq, an index made up mostly of tech companies, started the week of Oct 19 with a 1.1% jump as buyers came back after the previous week's drop. On Thursday, Oct 22, it fell 2.6%, its worst day since June. Investors were worried that AI companies are spending too much money, and oil prices also jumped. The index ended Friday at 25,955.34, down 0.7% for the week and its second losing week in a row, even though many companies are reporting strong results.
